findings.evidence: conflicting-candidate-integration-repair/design.md says "No mergeability. ... GitHub `mergeable` is not read." The proposal says the note "changes no state, posts no block and spends no attempt". The `_integrate` handler in publication_queue.py still re-raises `QueueEnvironmentError` after the note, with no transition. `derive_candidate` keeps state `blocked-retryable` and only swaps the reason text. The only new conflict tests (`test_conflict_outside_generated_files_needs_integration_repair`, `test_integration_repair_needed_routes_to_counted_integration_repair`) pin behavior that already existed. A candidate that GitHub reports as CONFLICTING but whose conflict `merge-tree` does not detect, or whose derived merge fails for environment reasons, still waits for checks that will not run. The narrowing is recorded as a coordinator decision ("variant A"), but it leaves the stated Requirement outcome unmet.
findings.summary: Requirement item 3 is not met. The change does not move a candidate that is waiting for required checks and has mergeable=CONFLICTING into integration-repair-pending. The one conflict case seen in practice, PR #837 with a generated-only conflict, still stays blocked-retryable. It gets only an `environment-error` note as its reason.
